raw.assessment: The incumbent provides telephone and in-person coordination, staffed key collection, and repeating bookings; eleven of twelve groups obtained weekly bookings. Its adequacy is unproven: acceptable windows and total needs are unknown, three conflicts occurred, and administration averaged 127.5 minutes weekly. Aggregate spare capacity and late or missed sessions suggest possible scheduling slack, not demonstrated usable availability. H4-O5 is a concrete limit: only one room has a piano, and blank equipment entries cannot establish interchangeability. Thus room-hours alone cannot explain or resolve refusals, especially the evening concentration.

openings.claim: Could reallocating inherited bookings meet documented needs within acceptable windows, or do simultaneous time and equipment requirements create an unavoidable shortage?
openings.delta: Distinguishes recoverable allocation mismatch from insufficient compatible capacity rather than treating unreserved hours as usable rehearsal time.
openings.prediction: Allocation mismatch predicts a feasible schedule meeting at least 90% of stated needs after acceptable windows and equipment are recorded. A compatibility shortage predicts remaining unmet demand even when inherited booking times can move within those windows.
openings.probe: Use short telephone or in-person conversations to record every group's total requested rehearsal duration, acceptable windows, and essential equipment, including needs currently met elsewhere. Attempt an eight-week allocation within existing staffed hours and equipment, preserving both performances and each requesting group's weekly 60-minute minimum. Record unmet compatible demand explicitly; do not count outside rehearsals as building provision or assume missed sessions are releasable.
assumptions: Groups can describe sufficiently stable requirements for eight weeks.
Moving inherited bookings requires agreement within recorded acceptable windows.
Feasibility remains unknown until requirements are collected.

openings.claim: One authoritative desk booking record, with numbered change acknowledgments and visibly dated copies, may reduce contradictory reservation expectations while retaining telephone and in-person changes.
openings.delta: Targets reservation-state disagreement independently of room capacity; it does not assume the two unexplained double arrivals share the documented calendar discrepancy's cause.
openings.prediction: Conflicts caused by conflicting record versions should decline; conflicts despite matching acknowledged records would indicate a different cause. Added bookkeeping may instead exceed the administration limit.
openings.probe: For eight weeks, record changes once in the authoritative ledger, acknowledge room and time through the requesting channel, and update dated copies. At each conflicting arrival compare each group's acknowledgment with the ledger. Track conflicts and all booking-administration minutes against fewer than two conflicts and a weekly average of at most 120 minutes.
assumptions: Desk staff and volunteer can consistently consult the same authoritative record.
Acknowledgments and copy updates fit available administrative time; this requires measurement.

raw.assessment: Recorded spare capacity does not establish usable capacity: acceptable windows, equipment needs and total demand are missing. Current observations do not establish the eight-week target's feasibility. Two hypotheses warrant bounded tests.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: allocating bookings from stated acceptable windows and equipment requirements, rather than inherited times, can meet more rehearsal needs within existing capacity.
openings.delta: Collect each group's weekly duration, acceptable windows and necessary equipment by phone or in person. Protect the two performances and each requesting group's weekly 60-minute entitlement, then allocate additional requested time; do not count an unwanted shorter session as a met need.
openings.prediction: If flexibility or room substitution is sufficient, a proposed allocation will accommodate previously declined needs without displacing protected access. If demand remains incompatible after collecting windows, this mechanism is insufficient.
openings.probe: Use the short contact conversations to construct one candidate week before changing reservations. Compare the share of stated needs fully met against the inherited schedule using the same demand data. Check equipment, entitlement and performance constraints; obtain agreement to changed times and track outcomes over eight weeks.
assumptions: Some groups accept alternative times or rooms.
Intake and allocation can fit within the total two-hour weekly administration average.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: recording each accepted booking or change once in a designated master calendar and confirming its room, date and time will reduce access conflicts and correction work.
openings.delta: Keep telephone and desk requests. Give each reservation a reference, amend its master entry before confirming, and mark the online copy with its update time. Use the master entry for key handoff.
openings.prediction: Calendar disagreements should disappear when the master is consulted; continuing conflicts despite matching confirmed entries would indicate causes beyond calendar synchronization.
openings.probe: For eight weeks, record each conflict's confirmed reservation details, master entry and mirror state. Measure total administration time, including updates and confirmations, and compare with the observed weeks; success requires fewer than two conflicts and an average at most 120 minutes.
assumptions: Existing desk staff can consult the master during current staffed hours.
Confirmation and correction savings offset the added recording effort.

openings.claim: Reallocating inherited bookings from stated needs may recover usable capacity.
openings.discriminator: Feasible compatible allocation indicates mismatch; residual incompatible demand indicates shortage despite aggregate slack.
openings.fit: Preserves C1-C4: two rooms, existing 24 staffed hours/equipment, weekly requested 60-minute entitlement, telephone/in-person access, no fees, both performances.
openings.probe: Interview all contacts for total duration, acceptable windows, equipment and needs met elsewhere. Compare one candidate week with inherited bookings using identical demand, then assess eight-week allocation. Obtain agreement before moving bookings; track fully met needs toward 90%. Exclude unwanted shortening and outside rehearsals from building provision; do not assume missed sessions releasable or blank equipment entries interchangeable.
openings.uncertainty: Requirement stability, flexibility, piano compatibility and total administration cost remain unknown.

openings.claim: One authoritative booking record with acknowledgments may reduce contradictory expectations and correction work.
openings.discriminator: Version conflicts should decline; matching confirmed records with conflicting arrivals indicate another cause.
openings.fit: Preserves C1-C4 and telephone/desk changes; requires staff consultation within existing hours.
openings.probe: Amend numbered master entries before confirming room/date/time through the requesting channel; date copies and consult master at key handoff. Over eight weeks compare conflict acknowledgments, master and mirror; measure all administration including D1, confirmations and updates.
openings.uncertainty: Two double arrivals have unexplained causes; consistent consultation and net time savings are unproven.

post_distill.decision: Feasibility unproven. Test jointly against 90% needs met, fewer than two conflicts and average administration at most 120 minutes weekly over eight weeks.
